newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Saudi firms sign $15 mln food, textiles deal.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Saudi firms sign $15 mln food, textiles deal.

text.p: A Saudi Arabian company and Iran's largest economic conglomerate have signed agreements worth more than $15 million to cooperate in sectors including the food and textile industries, a Saudi newspaper said on Wednesday.

The daily al-Eqtisadiah quoted Ahmed Zeini, director general of the Saudi firm al-Faezin, as saying the agreement covered the production of fruit juices and also included cooperation in transportation, agriculture and joint ventures.

Iranian newspapers earlier said the accords with Iran's state-affiliated Bonyad-e Mostazafan va Janbazan (Foundation for the Deprived and War Disabled) also included cooperation in exporting fruit concentrates to Saudi Arabia and foodstuffs to Central Asia.
The foundation is also studying setting up flights and a shipping line to Saudi Arabia, the press reports said.
The agreements came amid an apparent thaw in relations between Iran and its largest Arab neighbour across the Gulf.
The foundation controls over 700 factories and firms in Iran, including an airline called Bon Air and a shipping line.

It was formed after the 1979 Islamic revolution with the goal of helping the poor, using a large part of the property seized from rich members of the old regime, including assets of the late Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
